clue.text: One's product is ground caught in digger

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for caught is placed inside the word for a digger

parts.note: a miner digs for coal or ore
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught down a hole, and their product is ground underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen grinder that turns meat into mince is defined by what it produces, ground meat.

parts.note: quite, as an emphatic reply of agreement, means totally or completely
wonderful means marvellous, superb

explanation.surface: Someone praises a programme as quite wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' points to the entry at 1-down, which completes 8-down; the puzzle's theme is British TV sitcoms, and this one is a 1990s comedy about two hard-living fashion women.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-reference to light 1 stands for a television programme, and this is a well-known British sitcom title.

clue.text: Memorial film on canines, for example

definitions.meaning: a commemorative tablet fixed to a wall marking a person or event
the sticky bacterial deposit that coats teeth such as canines

explanation.surface: A memorial film is made about dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a commemorative wall tablet and the dental deposit forming a layer on teeth.

clue.text: While editor flabbergasted, ET leaving space rocket?

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was walking'

indicators.note: flabbergasted means stunned into confusion, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor is stunned when the alien ET departs aboard a spaceship.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself cryptic: with ET taken out of 'rocket', 'space rocket' leaves 'space rock'. The surface pictures the film alien flying away.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rocky body orbiting the Sun is literally a rock in space.

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the word is lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

explanation.surface: A monster is thereby raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairytale giant that eats people is a classic monster.

clue.text: Pervert hopes to occupy seat for Tom's entertainment?

indicators.note: to occupy says the rearranged letters fill the inside of the church seat

parts.note: a pew is a bench seat in a church

indicators.note: to pervert is to twist or corrupt, so the following word is bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A deviant hopes to sit in a church bench while watching a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' looks like a noun but is a verb signalling the anagram. A Peeping Tom is a voyeur, so this coin-slot booth is his idea of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peeping Tom is a voyeur, so a coin-in-slot erotic booth would be his kind of entertainment.

clue.text: Masses brought up with musical spirit

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s hippie stage musical
balls is slang for courage or spirit

explanation.surface: Lots of people are raised on a spirited musical diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masses brought up' sounds like people being raised; it means lumps a cat coughs up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats regurgitate compact clumps of swallowed fur, which are masses brought up.

clue.text: King in Texas city finds cuckoo

indicators.note: in places the chess abbreviation for king within the city name

parts.note: Waco is a city in central Texas
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A monarch visiting a Texan city turns out to be a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is slang for crazy, and so is this informal American word.

clue.text: Push in letter for audition, then start

indicators.note: for audition means the letter is taken as it is heard, not as written

parts.note: the letter Q, said out loud, sounds like a line of waiting people
to start is to jump in surprise

explanation.surface: Someone sends a letter in for an audition and then gets going.
explanation.definitionFit: To push in is to barge ahead of others waiting in line, an idiom for cutting the line.

parts.note: a tune is a song or melody

explanation.surface: Someone takes a chance on a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune means luck or chance, as in leaving things to fortune.

indicators.note: amend says one letter of the ordinal is altered to make a new word
the nucleus is the central letter of the five-letter ordinal, the one that changes

parts.note: fifth is an ordinal number, like first or second

explanation.surface: A request to amend the core of some ordinal reveals smut.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle F of FIFTH is altered; the clue does not name the replacement L, which the definition must supply. There may be a nod to taking the Fifth Amendment.
explanation.definitionFit: Filth is obscene or smutty material, so obscenities collectively; the query marks a loose plural.

clue.text: Drunk fine to go to hen party, then 1

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and muddled, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: a rave is a big dance party

explanation.surface: A tipsy woman is fit to go on to a hen night, then out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' shuffles FINE TO GO TO HEN into the first thirteen letters, then RAVE ends it. A hen party is a British bride's pre-wedding night out with her female friends. '1' is the theme: a British sitcom about grumpy pensioner Victor Meldrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Light 1 stands for a television programme, and this is a well-known BBC sitcom title.

clue.text: Ten plebeians somehow able to grow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged by some unstated method, in a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Ten common people manage somehow to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges X (Roman ten) with the letters of PLEBEIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expansible is capable of being expanded, so able to grow larger.

clue.text: Rows with fierce animals no good

indicators.note: no says the abbreviation for good is absent from the big cats

parts.note: tigers are fierce big cats

explanation.surface: Rows break out involving fierce animals that are no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows set one above another, as in a theatre or a wedding cake.

indicators.note: say means the word is to be heard, not read as spelt

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks with its tongue

explanation.surface: Someone makes a mistake with the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or minor mistake, as in a lapse of memory.

definitions.meaning: a hot oat cereal eaten in the morning
light 1 stands for a sitcom, here the prison comedy starring Ronnie Barker

explanation.surface: A morning meal is pitched as a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an oat breakfast dish and the British prison sitcom of the 1970s, prison slang for time served.

clue.text: Sheep enclosure collie emptied for a little bread

parts.note: a tup is a ram
a pen is a fenced enclosure for animals

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside letters, leaving just the first and last

explanation.surface: A sheepdog is removed from a sheep pen, all for a small sum.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money; two old British pennies made this small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and two old pence is only a little of it.

clue.text: Piece of soap is teeny, but it's slippery

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tiny bar of soap is a slippery thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepared ski run is packed snow, slippery underfoot by design.

clue.text: Ben has toe to accelerator certainly to increase speed

parts.note: Ben is followed by Hur in the title of the film Ben-Hur

indicators.note: the toe is the end of a foot, so toe to picks the final letter of the next word

parts.note: yup is casual for yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Ben puts his toe to the accelerator to go faster.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a move on is to go faster, the phrasal verb meaning to speed up.

clue.text: No cutting trumps: these decide the outcome

indicators.note: cutting means the word slices into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: in card games, to ruff is to play a trump

explanation.surface: A card player refuses to cut, while trumps settle the game.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games, to ruff is to play a trump.
explanation.definitionFit: Deciding contests held after a tie or inconclusive vote settle who wins.

definitions.meaning: light 1 stands for a sitcom, here the 1970s one about a seedy landlord
moisture creeping upward through brickwork from the ground

explanation.surface: A programme climbs up the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a building fault where ground moisture creeps up walls, and the Leonard Rossiter sitcom.

indicators.note: appearing in says the time letter and the shuffled number go inside the craze

parts.note: a fad is a passing craze

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the number word is mixed up

parts.note: the number three written as a word

explanation.surface: A programme of the time, a funny trio, appears in a craze.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' here is just the number word, not a cross-reference, and 'funny' turns THREE into HERTE. The sitcom is about Irish priests on Craggy Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Light 1 stands for a television programme, and this is a well-known Channel 4 sitcom about a priest.

parts.note: players who run the ball past opponents, or babies who slobber and need bibs at mealtimes

explanation.definitionFit: Footballers who run with the ball at their feet do this, and drooling infants wear bibs.

indicators.note: in a down clue standing means upright, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single politician stands for election on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island east of Java.

definitions.meaning: warms up, with the dropped h of a Cockney accent
slang for grub, things to eat

explanation.surface: Someone heats up food.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping the h from a word for warming gives the slang for food, and the Cockney accent drops it.

definitions.meaning: a bump of packed snow found on a ski run, the answer to 20

explanation.surface: A tycoon goes skiing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a business magnate and a mound of snow on a ski slope.

clue.text: Uncle of barmy books going the same way

indicators.note: barmy is British slang for mad, so these letters go wild

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A dotty uncle with his books heads the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle of barmy books' reads as a dotty relative's library, but 'barmy' is only the anagram signal and 'books' is the usual New Testament abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Confluent streams flow together, merging in one direction.
